added_claim_errors: Ties the no-penalty delay to the employer being over 20 employees ("That makes your group plan primary, and it lets you delay Part B"). Employer size is not a condition of the SEP; the key calls this imprecise but minor.

"you might need a Part D plan, and possibly Part B to get it": misleading. Part D needs Part A or Part B, and premium-free Part A is enough, so non-creditable drug coverage gives no reason to take Part B.
"Save the CMS-L564 form (your employer fills it out)": imprecise. The enrollee completes Section A and the employer completes Section B.
"some do; most don't" (plans requiring Medicare at 65): unverifiable generalization, minor.

Ties the no-penalty delay to the 400-employee size ("That lets you delay Part B"; "Under 20 ... you'd want to enroll at 65"). The SEP does not depend on employer size; the key calls this imprecise but minor.

reasons: Both answers open by correcting the coworker's premise. Both give the 8-month SEP and the 10% lifetime penalty correctly, cover the HR questions and the HSA warning with the 6-month backdating, and neither states the exception for coverage ending during the IEP. A adds the 2026 premium of $202.90/month (about $2,435 a year) with a Federal Register link, which I opened and which confirms the figure. A also names CMS-L564 and the 2-month Part D window after coverage ends, so the person can act on it more fully. B correctly says COBRA does not extend the window and points to SHIP. But B gives no premium figure, uses a generic HR letter instead of CMS-L564, and never mentions the Part D timing. A has small imprecisions (who fills out L564, and "possibly Part B" for Part D), but its answer is more concrete and more complete overall.
